paragraphs.notes: The zh field holds the verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese; here the whole page body is a substituent enumeration table whose cells are chemical symbols and compound numbers, with no German prose in them at all, so zh and en are the same string. The page carries no Tabelle caption: the table begins on an earlier page and continues past this one, so the shared substituents and the drawn scaffold that govern these rows are not on this page. The column headers are printed with superscript locants (R with superscript 7a, 7b, 12 and 1); they are transcribed inline as R7a, R7b, R12 and R1 because the plain-text transcription has no superscripts, and likewise the subscript digits in CH2, SO2, CF3 and CH2CH2 are printed as subscripts and written inline here. Row 125 is the only row whose R1 is O-c-Pr and rows 150 and 151 are the only rows whose L is CH2CH2 and whose R1 is O-c-Hexyl; every other row on the page has L = CH2 and R1 = OCH2CF3. 'Pr' in PrSO2 is printed with no n- or i- prefix and is transcribed as printed, not resolved to n-propyl. A small stray ink mark sits directly above the O of OCH2CF3 in the R1 cell of row 126; it is a scan artifact and not a character or a prime. Faint short pencil-like ticks sit in the empty part of the Nr. cells of rows 126 and 145; they are also scan artifacts. The cell dividing rules between the Nr., R7a, R7b and R12 columns print as broken dotted lines on several rows, which is a print quality artifact and does not affect the cell contents.
